 Jagiroad College: Prospectus: 2021-22

                         A brief profile of the College
           Jagiroad College (the erstwhile Kapili Anchalik Mahavidyalaya) was established on 8th
 August, 1979. The College is located at Jagiroad in the Morigaon district of Assam, at a distance of
 nearly one hundred meters from the AH 2. The serene campus, spread over a spacious area of twenty-
 five bighas of land, is nestled by the picturesque Sonaikuchi Hill. Culturally it lies very close to Na-
 Khola—the abode of the Prince Regent of the ancient Kingdom of the Tiwas –one of the indigenous
 tribes of the state endowed with its distinctive traditional heritage. Jagiroad College was established by
 a group of foresighted and committed social-workers of the region. Shri Mahendra Ahom, the founder
 Principal played a pivotal role for seventeen years in the development of the College. With his
 dynamism, the College was able to attract students from the surrounding rural hinterlands who were
 mostly “first generation” learners belonging to the socio-economically disadvantaged and marginalized
 communities. Shri Ahom laid the foundation of the academic and infrastructural blue print of the
 College while inspiring the teachers to promote the cherished values of inclusiveness and equity without
 losing sight of qualitative parameters. During his tenure both the Arts and Science Streams of the
 College were brought under the “deficit-grant-in-aid” system of Government of Assam following
 affiliation of its programmes and courses by the Gauhati University and it became eligible for
 development grants under sections 2(f) and 12(b) of the UGC Act 1956.In 1997, Sri Ahom left to
 Nowgong College and on his resignation, Dr. Altafur Rahman has joined the College as the second
 permanent Principal and served for eight years between 2000 and 2008 and then as the President of the
 G.B. for five years. During Dr. Rahman’s tenure the College was accredited and assessed by the NAAC
 and career oriented professional programmes like MTM and PGDCA (under Gauhati University),
 distance education programmes under IGNOU, tie-up with NBIRT for promotion of entrepreneurship
 were introduced. He also worked towards further expansion of infrastructural facilities like construction
 of hostels, expansion of library and computer center. During Dr. Rahman’s tenure, the College also
 celebrated its Silver Jubilee in 2005 with enthusiasm and gaiety with active coordination of a large
 number of its alumni. That same year the College came under the ambit of the Assam College
 Employees (Provincialisation) Act, 2005. Besides Dr. Rahman, one of the former Vice Principals- Shri
 Utpalmoni Phukan served as the Principal-in-charge in two phases.
                                                                                                              2
          Dr. Bhaben Chandra Neog, the present Principal of the College has joined as the third
permanent Principal of the College in January, 2012 and started off his tenure by launching programmes
and courses like Bachelor in Commerce (B.Com. with both Major and General Courses). It is under the
initiative of Dr. Neog that the college has introduced a few innovative skill and employment -
generating programmes with financial support from the University Grants Commission (UGC). These
courses are included in two different schemes namely-Community College scheme and Bachelor of
Vocation (BVoc) scheme of the UGC. Of these, the Pulp and Paper Technology (PPT) and Fashion
Technology were introduced since 2015-16 under the Community College Scheme of UGC. But due to
the closure of the Nagaon Paper Mill of HPCL these courses have been discontinued from 2019-20
session.
         Under the Bachelor of Vocation (B.Voc.) scheme of UGC, the College has been imparting
B.Voc programme in (i) Retail Management (RTM)and (ii) Entertainment-Acting (ACT) since 2015-
16 academic session and (iii) Tourism and Hospitality Management (THM) programme from the
Academic Session 2018-19. All these have been running as three years Bachelor Degree Programmes
under the Gauhati University. Sector Skill Councils like Media and Entertainment Sector Skill Council
(MESC), Retailers Association Sector Skill Council (RASCI) and Tourism and Hospitality
Management Sector Skill Council (THSC) under the National Skill Development Council (NSDC)
evaluated the students studying in these Programmes for their skill components. As a part of skill
enhancement and employment centric commitments, the college has signed a number of Memorandums
of Understandings (MoUs) with different Industry partners/ Institutions to empower the students in skill
and related activities. Regional Govt. Film and Television Institute (RGFTI) located at Kahilipara,
Directorate of Tourism, Govt. of Assam extended their support to the students. They have encouraged
endeavours in implementing courses to generate skilled human resources for the benefit of society.
         During the last nine years, the college have seen many new additions in terms of academic as
well as in infrastructural fronts. Apart from regular courses and skill based courses, Distance Education
courses have also been introduced for the needy students. Those who could not avail their higher
educational need have been availing their dreams realized through the study cum exam centers of
IGNOU,KKHSOU and GU-IDOL located in the college. Since the college has puts utmost emphasis
upon infrastructural facilities, the process of up-gradation of the classrooms is underway and six
numbers of classrooms have already been upgraded with digital smart-boards. A Digital Language
Laboratory was added to the Computer department for students seeking development of English
language skills. A 50 kw Solar power plant was installed in the college to meet the shortage of power
supply for the smooth functioning of the academic and other day-to-day activities. The college has also
successfully established its digital library building. Since its early days, Jagiroad College has been in
the forefront in promoting inclusiveness and equity, adopting learner-friendly teaching-learning
mechanisms, academic exchanges and organizing seminars and conferences.
         In the past, the college has successfully organized annual/biennial sessions of NEIHA, NEIGS,
ACPC and AACEA apart from having regular calendar of seminars by the IQAC and hosting State and
National level seminars/webinars on different topics/subjects. Dr. Subhash Saha, a faculty of the
History department, carved a niche for himself as a multifaceted scholar-poet- social activist and was
engaged in Post Doctoral research till his untimely demise in 1994. Prof. Moloya Goswami, who has
retired from her service, bagged the Best Actress Award of the 37th National Film Awards in 1992 for
her stellar role in Jahnu Barua directed movie Firingoti (A Spark). She was also thrice nominated as a
member of the prestigious jury for the National Film Awards. Shri Tulshi Kr. Bordoloi, a retired faculty
of the History Department and a former President of the Tiwa Mathonlai Tokhra (Tiwa Sahitya Sabha)
acts as a key resource person regarding studies in the cultural and literary heritage of the Tiwas. Dr.

 Poban Ch. Gogoi and Dr. Khagen Sarma, both retired Associated Professors and Ex Heads of Education
and Geography Departments respectively contributed their skills in cultural arena for the benefit of the
society. Dr. Gogoi established a Music College just in front of the College and Dr. Sarma established a
Satriya Sangeet Vidyalaya and helped spread the Vaishnavite culture for the last twenty five years for
the greater cause of the society and common people.
         Teachers of the college are also committed and engaged in Major and Minor research projects
besides being awarded Ph.D. and M.Phil. degrees from universities of repute and institutes of national
importance. A section of the teachers are also actively engaged in local literary, cultural and sports
organizations besides offering assistance and consultancy to community based organizations. Sections
of the non-teaching staff too are sincere and committed in their services.
         With its pleasant and peaceful teaching-learning ambience the college campus is an ideal place
to study. The College also has a supportive alumni association, many of whom have successfully
shaped and carved out their careers in different fields including, education, health, management, society
and research areas. Additionally, the College has excellent infrastructural facilities, a reasonably high
rate of gender parity, a wide array of full time academic programmes and courses ranging from Higher
Secondary to Master in Tourism Management, also offers excellent support for affordable and broad-
based Distance Education under IGNOU, KKHSOU and IDOL of Gauhati University. The College
also boasts of a well-stocked and updated library with nearly thirty thousand books, varied schemes of
scholarships for learners, seminars and conferences, grievance redressal mechanism, wide range of
CCA activities. It is gradually and uniquely poised to scale higher in the contours of Higher Education
of Assam. The institution has all along been trying to evolve its own quality-sustenance mechanism in
its pursuit to achieve academic excellence. The college has been able to yield B+ grade with 2.71
CGPA in the second cycle of its assessment by NAAC in 2016.The department of Biotechnology, GoI
has approved and funded the DBT Star College Scheme grant to this college in 2019-20 through which
the college hopes to enhancing science education both theoretically and practically.



                Jagiroad College - in India’s Best Colleges list:
     (As per India Today MDRA survey report for three consecutive years: 2019, 2020, 2021)

         Few vital points usually arise while considering National Ranking of an Institution. What is the
present status of any stream of a higher education institution (HEI) in comparison to the rest of the
similar institutions in the country? How can an HEI justify itself as this or that type of Institute or how
one can compare it’s status or rank with other similar institutions? NAAC is an autonomous body for
assessment and accreditation of HEIs every five years. Apart from NAAC, is there any other national
testing agency to annually evaluate or assess any HEI in our country? Although the National Institution
Ranking Framework (NIRF) had started the process by working and ranking institutions since 2014-15,
parameter wise limited scopes available for stream-wise participation for many institutions. From that
perspective, the national survey conducted by the “India Today group” has been conducting Best
College Survey Ranking in India (now-a-days known as MDRA-India Today National Best College
Ranking Survey) for the last twenty-five years holds a valid reason to participate. Last year they have
conducted the survey covering 9 broad aspects in 9 different sections including a special section for
covid-19 impact assessments.
         Our college has participated in their survey since 2019 with a clear intention to check the
National status or National Position/Rank among hundreds of other participating institutions. To our
surprise and as per the MDRA-India Today National Best Colleges Ranking survey report, in the year

                                                                                                              4
 2019, the college had emerged as one of the best colleges in our country. In that year, Jagiroad College
held National Ranks at 112, 112 and 141 for its Arts, Science and Commerce streams respectively.
Again in 2020, the three streams of the college secured ranks 127(Arts), 132(Science) and
137(Commerce) in-spite-of Covid-19 pandemic. In 2020 survey report, the Commerce stream had
emerged as 3rd College in India having lowest tuition fee. Further, despite the second wave of Covid-19
pandemic in 2021, the college has yet again established itself as one of the best by holding national
ranks at 155(Arts), 149(Science) and 158(Commerce). Thus, albeit some ups and downs, the three
streams of the college has been maintaining national ranking in that survey ever since its first
participation. Thus, the National Ranking to the college that too for three successive years is really a
matter of pride for all the fraternity of the college.

   “One District One Green Champion” award-2021 to the college
        The college proudly announces that under the “Swachhta Action Plan 2020-21” of the Ministry
of Education, GoI, this college has been awarded the prestigious “One District One Green Champion”
award by the Mahatma Gandhi National Council of Rural Education’s recently. In the award list, this
college has been enlisted at 24 out of 400 other colleges/Universities/NITs/IITs in India. This
announcement greatly encourages the college fraternity towards maintaining clean and green
environment with social commitments. Thus, the involvement of the college family in areas other than
academic gains momentum and expects to be more vigilant and socially conscious institution.



                  DBT Star College Scheme Grant
             A Scheme for Strengthening UG Science Education
         This college has received the Star College Scheme Grant of the Department of Biotechnology
(DBT), Government of India in 2019 for three years. Under this scheme, the DBT has sanctioned grants
to the following departments, viz. Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics, Botany and
Zoology. With the grants from DBT, the College has already established a central Instrumentation
facility centre with sophisticated instruments which was inaugurated by Dr. Deepak Majumdar, IAS,
Secretary, Higher Education, Govt. of Assam & Mission Director, RUSA, Assam on 4th December,
2020.
         This Star College Scheme has been initiated by DBT in 2008 to support colleges and
universities offering undergraduate science education in order to improve science teaching across the
country. DBT is committed to the value of –i) Pursuit of excellence, ii) Academic and intellectual
freedom, iii) Creativity and innovation, iv) Diversity, v) Cooperation and Communication and vi)
Accountability. Therefore, DBT has launched this scheme for improving critical thinking and hands on
experimental work at undergraduate (college) level in science. It is expected to encourage more students
to take up higher education in science. DBT identifies colleges with ambition and potential for
excellence and provides academic and physical infrastructures for achieving excellence, exposing
students to a wide array of opportunities. Apart from financial support, our college has benefited and
continues to benefit tremendously from guidance received during Advisory Committee meetings,
mentoring, task force meetings and learning from peers in other colleges.

 Objective of the Scheme-
 ● To strengthen the academic and physical infrastructure for achieving excellence in teaching and
     training.
 ● To enhance the quality of learning and teaching process to stimulate original thinking through
     hands on exposure to experimental work and participation in summer school.
 ● To promote networking and strengthen ties with neighbouring institutions and other laboratories.
 ● To conduct specialised training programme for faculty development for optimizing technical
     capabilities.
 ● To increase capabilities of core instrumentation resources by procuring new equipments and
     upgrading existing facilities.
 ● To provide excess and exposure to students to research laboratories and industries in the country.
 ● To help in devising standard curricula and standard operating procedures (SOPs) / kits for
     practicals.
         Under this DBT Star College scheme grant, the college has organized several programmes in
the past two years such as workshops, popular talks, summer schools in the feeder schools and exposure
visits to IITG and Tezpur University and Gauhati University. During the period of current lockdown
due to the second wave of Covid-19 pandemic, the College is organising virtual webinar programmes
with financial support from the DBT fund. These are- webinar lectures on (i) “Ecosystem Restoration:
prospects and Challenges in India” by eminent Science Communicator Dr. Arup Kr. Misra, Former
Director, ASTEC and Associate Professor of AEC organised on the occasion of World Environment
Day, (ii) “An Introduction to IPR and Issues related to Academic Community” by Dr. Mayank Pratap
from the School of Law, Banaras Hindu University, (iii) “Drosophila as a model for Class room
Studies” by S.S. Bhatnagar awardee Professor Dr. S.C Lakhotia from the Department of Zoology, BHU
and (iv) “Epigenetic modulators as chemotherapeutic targets” by Dr. Rohini Muthuswami, Assoc.
Prof., School of Life Sciences, JNU, New Delhi are some of these initiatives. Apart from those, a
twoday workshop on PYTHON and a four-day virtual hands-on training programme on “Statistical
Software-SPSS for Data Analysis” etc. were also organised by the departments with the aid of DBT
Star College Scheme.

SCOPE
Retail industry is the second largest employment generation sector after agriculture whereas Media &
Entertainment industry is in the third position. Retail and Media & Entertainment are two of the fastest
growing industries in the world. In the North-East India both the sectors are growing as rapidly as
anywhere in the world. There is therefore a growing need of skilled personnel and professionals to meet

other related services.
         After successful completion of three year B.Voc., Acting students can work in different sectors
relating to Media & Entertainment such as films, T.V, theatre, mobile theatre, radio, advertisements,
animation etc. as film, television, theatre actors, radio artistes, Voice over artistes, dubbing artistes,
production, etc.
         At the end of three year B.Voc., Retail Management students will be able to work in different
profiles as Team member, Team leader, Cashier, Ware House executive, MIS executive, Store
Manager, Floor Manager, Visual Merchandiser, Asstt. Department Manager, Department Manager, etc.
         On successful completion of the B.Voc., Tourism and Hospitality Management students can
secure jobs as a Front office Manager, Food and Beverage Manager, Resort Manager, Restaurant
Manager, Event Supervisor, Airline/Cruise Consultant, Hotel Operation and Entrepreneur etc.

performance evaluation, assessment and accreditation and quality up-gradation. According to National
Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), Bangalore, it is mandatory, that all high educational
institute should have a functional IQAC. Quality enhancement in a college is a continuous process and so,
this cell becomes a part of the institution’s functioning system and work towards fulfilling the objectives
of the institution and achieving the goals. It disseminates its responsibilities through the formations of
different cells. With the help of all stakeholders IQAC perform different activities towards teaching-
learning and evaluation, skill orientation, career orientation of students. It takes necessary action to expose
the students to the modern ICT based knowledge, organizes popular lecture by academicians from advance
institutions, lecture for career guidance, skill learning etc. It encourages innovative changes, encourage
different training programmes to build up competence, augments learner centric environment for quality
education. Moreover, IQAC also organizes workshops, seminars for academic advancement of the faculty
members, stimulate the academic environment for promotion of quality of teaching- learning and research
in higher education, undertake       quality-related research studies and initiate faulty exchange
programme. The career guidance and placement cell organizes the career counseling sessions in the
campus and taken care of the placement, internship and On-Job Training (OJT) of students. In collaborate
with all stakeholders including alumni of the institution, IQAC do work for the quality promotion and
sustenance. It adapts a system of continuous documentation to create data base, prepares the Annual
Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) of the institution and taken care of its timely submission to NAAC.
      Jagiroad College has a functional IQAC with a permanent office room and continuously doing its
activities for the all round development of students and institution as a whole.
